questions.text: Which is the longest river in the world?
questions.explanation: The Nile, flowing north through north-eastern Africa, is traditionally regarded as the world's longest river at roughly 6,650 km.

questions.text: Which is the highest mountain in the world above sea level?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest, on the Nepal-Tibet border, rises to 8,849 metres, making it the highest peak above sea level.

questions.text: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explanation: The Sahara, covering most of North Africa, is the world's largest hot desert at about 9.2 million square kilometres.

questions.text: Which is the largest ocean in the world by area?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean covers more area than all the continents combined, making it the largest of the world's oceans.

questions.text: Which is the largest lake in the world by surface area?
questions.explanation: The Caspian Sea, bordered by five countries, is classified as a lake and is the largest inland body of water on Earth.

questions.text: Which is the largest island in the world?
questions.explanation: Greenland, an autonomous territory of Denmark, is the world's largest island, as Australia is classified as a continent rather than an island.

questions.text: Which is the largest continent by area?
questions.explanation: Asia covers about 30% of Earth's land area, making it the largest continent by a wide margin.

questions.text: Which is the smallest continent by landmass?
questions.explanation: Australia is the smallest of the world's continents by total landmass.

questions.text: Which is the largest country in the world by total area?
questions.explanation: Russia spans roughly 17.1 million square kilometres across Europe and Asia, making it the largest country by area.

questions.text: Which is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.explanation: Vatican City, an independent city-state enclosed within Rome, covers only about 0.44 square kilometres.

questions.text: Which is the largest peninsula in the world?
questions.explanation: The Arabian Peninsula, bordered by the Red Sea, Arabian Sea, and Persian Gulf, is the world's largest peninsula.

questions.text: The Mariana Trench, home to the deepest known point in the world's oceans, lies in which body of water?
questions.explanation: The Mariana Trench in the western Pacific contains the Challenger Deep, the deepest known point in any ocean.

questions.text: Which waterfall has the world's highest uninterrupted single drop?
questions.explanation: Angel Falls in Venezuela has an uninterrupted drop of 807 metres, the greatest of any waterfall in the world.

questions.text: Which is the world's largest coral reef system?
questions.explanation: The Great Barrier Reef off Australia's coast stretches over 2,300 km, making it the largest coral reef system on Earth.

questions.text: Which is the longest mountain range on land?
questions.explanation: The Andes run about 7,000 km along the western edge of South America, making them the longest continental mountain range.

questions.text: Which is the largest bay in the world by area?
questions.explanation: The Bay of Bengal, part of the northeastern Indian Ocean, is the world's largest bay by area.

questions.text: Which is the largest gulf in the world by area?
questions.explanation: The Gulf of Mexico, bordered by the United States, Mexico, and Cuba, is the largest gulf in the world.

questions.text: Which country contains the world's largest archipelago?
questions.explanation: Indonesia is made up of more than 17,000 islands, making it the largest archipelago in the world.

questions.text: Which is the largest tropical rainforest in the world?
questions.explanation: The Amazon Rainforest, spanning much of the Amazon Basin in South America, is the largest tropical rainforest on Earth.

questions.text: Which city is generally regarded as the highest national capital in the world?
questions.explanation: La Paz, Bolivia's seat of government, sits at roughly 3,640 metres above sea level, the highest elevation of any national capital.

questions.text: Which is the world's deepest lake?
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal in Siberia reaches a depth of about 1,642 metres, making it the deepest lake on Earth.

questions.text: Which is the smallest of the world's oceans?
questions.explanation: The Arctic Ocean, surrounding the North Pole, is the smallest and shallowest of the world's oceans.

questions.text: Which is the largest river delta in the world?
questions.explanation: The Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta, spanning Bangladesh and India, is the largest river delta in the world.

questions.text: Which country has the longest coastline in the world?
questions.explanation: Canada's coastline, including its many islands and inlets, measures over 200,000 km, the longest of any country.

questions.text: Which is the largest landlocked country in the world?
questions.explanation: Kazakhstan, in Central Asia, has no coastline and is the largest landlocked country in the world by area.

questions.text: Which is the longest man-made wall in the world?
questions.explanation: The Great Wall of China, built and extended over centuries, stretches for thousands of kilometres across northern China.

questions.text: Which is the world's tallest free-standing mountain, measured from base to peak?
questions.explanation: Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania rises about 5,895 metres from its base as an isolated volcanic massif, unlike Everest which sits within a mountain range.

questions.text: Which is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area?
questions.explanation: Lake Superior, one of North America's Great Lakes, covers about 82,100 square kilometres, the largest freshwater lake by area.

questions.text: Which plateau, often called the 'Roof of the World', is the highest and most extensive plateau on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Tibetan Plateau, bordered by the Himalayas, has an average elevation above 4,500 metres, the highest of any large plateau.

questions.text: Which continent is classified as the world's largest desert by area, owing to its extremely low precipitation?
questions.explanation: By the climatological definition of a desert as a region of very low precipitation, Antarctica, covering about 14 million square kilometres, is the largest desert in the world.

questions.text: Who is credited as the first person to reach the North Pole?
questions.explanation: American explorer Robert Peary was recognised by the National Geographic Society and the US Congress as the first person to reach the North Pole, in 1909.

questions.text: Who was the first person to reach the South Pole?
questions.explanation: Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen led the first expedition to reach the South Pole, on 14 December 1911.

questions.text: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the lunar surface on 20 July 1969 during the Apollo 11 mission, becoming the first person to walk on the Moon.

questions.text: Who was the first human to travel into space?
questions.explanation: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space when he orbited the Earth aboard Vostok 1 on 12 April 1961.

questions.text: Who was the first woman to travel into space?
questions.explanation: Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman in space when she flew aboard Vostok 6 in June 1963.

questions.text: Who was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean?
questions.explanation: Amelia Earhart completed a solo nonstop flight across the Atlantic in 1932, the first woman to achieve this.

questions.text: Whose expedition was the first to circumnavigate the globe, even though he died before it was completed?
questions.explanation: Ferdinand Magellan led the expedition that first circumnavigated the globe, but he died in the Philippines in 1521; his crew, under Juan Sebastian Elcano, completed the voyage in 1522.

questions.text: Along with Tenzing Norgay, who was the first person to reach the summit of Mount Everest?
questions.explanation: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay became the first climbers to reach the summit of Mount Everest, on 29 May 1953.

questions.text: Who was the first President of the United States?
questions.explanation: George Washington served as the first President of the United States, taking office in 1789.

questions.text: Who was the first woman in the world to serve as a Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: Sirimavo Bandaranaike of Ceylon (now Sri Lanka) became the world's first woman Prime Minister when she took office in 1960.

questions.text: Which country was the first to grant women the right to vote in national elections?
questions.explanation: New Zealand became the first self-governing country to grant women the right to vote in national elections, in 1893.

questions.text: Who was the first person to walk in space?
questions.explanation: Soviet cosmonaut Alexei Leonov performed the first spacewalk in March 1965.

questions.text: Which living creature was the first to orbit the Earth?
questions.explanation: The Soviet dog Laika became the first living creature to orbit the Earth, aboard Sputnik 2 in 1957.

questions.text: Along with Don Walsh, who was the first person to reach the Challenger Deep, the ocean's deepest known point?
questions.explanation: Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh reached the bottom of the Challenger Deep in the bathyscaphe Trieste in 1960, the first to do so.

questions.text: Which country launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite to orbit the Earth?
questions.explanation: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 in October 1957, the first artificial satellite to orbit the Earth.

questions.text: Which mission first landed astronauts on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Apollo 11 carried the first crew to land on the Moon in July 1969.

questions.text: Who was the first European explorer to reach India by an all-sea route?
questions.explanation: Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama reached Calicut, India, by sea in 1498, opening a direct maritime route from Europe.

questions.text: Which country was the first to test a nuclear weapon?
questions.explanation: The United States conducted the first nuclear weapon test, code-named Trinity, in New Mexico in July 1945.

questions.text: Who completed the first solo, nonstop transatlantic flight?
questions.explanation: Charles Lindbergh flew the Spirit of St. Louis nonstop from New York to Paris in 1927, the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight.

questions.text: Along with Peter Habeler, who was the first person to summit Mount Everest without supplemental oxygen?
questions.explanation: Reinhold Messner and Peter Habeler reached the summit of Everest without bottled oxygen in 1978, a feat many had believed impossible.

questions.text: Who was the first person to sail single-handed and nonstop around the world?
questions.explanation: British sailor Robin Knox-Johnston completed the first solo, nonstop circumnavigation by sea in 1969.

questions.text: Who was the first person to reach the Challenger Deep alone?
questions.explanation: Filmmaker and explorer James Cameron piloted the Deepsea Challenger to the bottom of the Challenger Deep alone in 2012.

questions.text: Which institution is widely recognised as the oldest continually operating degree-granting university in the world?
questions.explanation: The University of Al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, Morocco, founded in 859 AD, is recognised by UNESCO and Guinness World Records as the oldest existing degree-granting university.

questions.text: Which city hosted the first modern Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: Athens hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896, reviving the ancient Greek tradition.

questions.text: Who was the first woman known to have circumnavigated the globe?
questions.explanation: Jeanne Baret, a French botanist who disguised herself as a man to join Louis Antoine de Bougainville's expedition, became the first woman to circumnavigate the globe, between 1766 and 1769.

questions.text: Who is credited with inventing the telephone?
questions.explanation: Alexander Graham Bell was granted the first patent for the telephone in 1876 and is credited as its inventor.

questions.text: Who is credited with developing the first practical incandescent light bulb?
questions.explanation: Thomas Edison developed a commercially practical, long-lasting incandescent light bulb in 1879.

questions.text: Who invented the printing press with movable metal type in Europe?
questions.explanation: Johannes Gutenberg introduced the movable-type printing press in Europe around 1440, revolutionising the spread of printed material.

questions.text: Which physicist developed the theory of relativity?
questions.explanation: Albert Einstein published the special theory of relativity in 1905 and the general theory of relativity in 1915.

questions.text: Which Scottish engineer is credited with developing the television?
questions.explanation: John Logie Baird gave the first public demonstration of a working television system in 1926.

questions.text: Who is credited with developing Morse code?
questions.explanation: Samuel Morse, along with Alfred Vail, developed Morse code for use with the electric telegraph in the 1830s.

questions.text: Who invented the World Wide Web?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN.

questions.text: Which Swedish chemist and engineer invented dynamite?
questions.explanation: Alfred Nobel invented dynamite in 1867, which formed the basis of his fortune and later funded the Nobel Prizes.

questions.text: Which Scottish bacteriologist discovered penicillin?
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 after noticing it killed bacteria in a contaminated culture dish.

questions.text: Which brothers are credited with the first successful powered, controlled airplane flight?
questions.explanation: Orville and Wilbur Wright achieved the first sustained, controlled, powered flight in December 1903.

questions.text: Which Italian inventor is credited with pioneering long-distance radio transmission?
questions.explanation: Guglielmo Marconi developed practical long-distance radio transmission and won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1909 for this work.

questions.text: Which English physician developed the first vaccine, against smallpox?
questions.explanation: Edward Jenner developed the smallpox vaccine in 1796, laying the foundation for the field of immunology.

questions.text: Whose improvements to the steam engine made it efficient enough for widespread industrial use?
questions.explanation: James Watt's design improvements in the 1770s greatly increased the efficiency of the steam engine, driving the Industrial Revolution.

questions.text: Which Russian chemist created the periodic table of elements?
questions.explanation: Dmitri Mendeleev published the periodic table of elements in 1869, arranging elements by atomic weight and properties.

questions.text: Which naturalist proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection?
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection in his 1859 book 'On the Origin of Species'.

questions.text: Which scientist formulated the law of universal gravitation?
questions.explanation: Isaac Newton formulated the law of universal gravitation, published in his 1687 work 'Principia Mathematica'.

questions.text: In which year were the first Nobel Prizes awarded?
questions.explanation: The first Nobel Prizes, in Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, and Peace, were awarded in 1901, five years after Alfred Nobel's death.

questions.text: The Nobel Prizes were established through the will of which Swedish inventor?
questions.explanation: Alfred Nobel's 1895 will directed that his fortune fund annual prizes recognising achievements in several fields.

questions.text: Who was the first person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences?
questions.explanation: Marie Curie won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 and the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1911, the first person honoured in two different sciences.

questions.text: Which Nobel Prize category was not part of Alfred Nobel's original 1895 will and was added later?
questions.explanation: The Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences was established by Sweden's central bank in 1968 and first awarded in 1969, decades after Nobel's original five prizes.

questions.text: Which English engineer is known as the 'Father of Railways' for building the first successful steam locomotives?
questions.explanation: George Stephenson built the pioneering steam locomotives Locomotion and Rocket, earning him the title 'Father of Railways'.

questions.text: Which physicist discovered X-rays and won the first Nobel Prize in Physics?
questions.explanation: Wilhelm Rontgen discovered X-rays in 1895 and was awarded the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901 for the discovery.

questions.text: Along with James Watson, who co-discovered the double-helix structure of DNA?
questions.explanation: James Watson and Francis Crick proposed the double-helix structure of DNA in 1953, drawing partly on X-ray data from Rosalind Franklin.

questions.text: Which Dutch spectacle-maker is credited with inventing the first telescope?
questions.explanation: Hans Lippershey filed the first patent application for a telescope in 1608; Galileo later improved the design and used it for astronomy.

questions.text: Which American virologist developed the first successful polio vaccine?
questions.explanation: Jonas Salk developed the first successful inactivated polio vaccine, announced in 1955.
